env.noKernel: Install {{lang}} with its Jupyter kernel to see variables here.

plots.emptyBody: Plots from R and Python appear here, styled to match your theme.

layout.label: Layout
layout.analysisDesc: Four panes: editor, console, environment, plots
layout.developmentDesc: Large editor, side panels, console below

commands.debugStart: Debug: Start debugging the current file / Continue

onboarding.welcomeBody: One place for R and Python: editor, consoles, variables and plots side by side.
onboarding.envBody: DataForge looks for installed versions and their Jupyter kernels. There's nothing to configure by hand.
onboarding.startBody: You can change the layout at any time from the title bar or the command palette.

lsp.title: Language servers
lsp.idle: Starts when you open a file

data.sortHint: Click to sort, Shift+click to add a sort key
data.invalidFilter: Not a valid filter for this column
data.noRows: No rows match the current filters
data.goneBody: The variable was removed or the session restarted. Close this tab or create the variable again.

files.noProjectBody: Open a folder to browse its files. Kernels then run in that folder, with the project’s own R and Python environments.
files.deleteBody: You can restore it from the system trash.
files.deleteFailed: Couldn't move it to the trash

packages.notCheckedBody: Checking contacts the package repository and may take a moment.
packages.removeBody: The package is uninstalled from this environment.
packages.renvNoLock: no renv.lock yet — snapshot to create it

help.notFoundBody: Check the spelling, or search with ?? / the search box.
help.emptyBody: Search above, type ?topic in the R console or help(x) in Python.
help.f1: opens help for the word under the cursor

preview.firstRenderBody: Code chunks run in a fresh session, so this can take a few seconds.
preview.emptyTitle: Live preview for Quarto and R Markdown
preview.emptyBody: Open a .qmd or .Rmd file and render it. While this panel shows the document, every save renders it again.
preview.needQuarto: Quarto is needed to render .qmd files. Install it from https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/ (or: pip install quarto-cli), then render again.
preview.needTool: Rendering needs Quarto or R with the rmarkdown package.

git.discardBody: Modified files go back to their last staged/committed state; new files are moved to the trash.
git.nothingStagedBody: Stage all changes and commit them?
git.dirtySwitchBody: Git carries the changes over when it can, and stops if they would be overwritten.
git.badBranch: “{{name}}” is not a valid branch name
git.noRemote: This repository has no remote to push to
git.abortMergeBody: The branch returns to its state before the merge; conflict resolutions are lost.
git.mergeReady: All conflicts resolved — commit to finish the merge
git.clean: No changes — the working tree is clean
git.noProjectBody: Open a project folder to see its Git status here.
git.missingBody: Install Git (git-scm.com) and restart DataForge to use version control.
git.notRepoBody: “{{name}}” is not under version control yet.

terminal.exited: [process exited with code {{code}} — press Enter to restart]

debug.runningHint: Running — values appear when execution pauses
debug.noBreakpointsHint: Click left of a line number (or press F9) in an R or Python file to add one.
debug.intro: Set breakpoints in an R or Python file and press F5. The script runs in the console's session, so you inspect the same variables you work with. Breakpoints also stop functions you call from the console.
debug.notDebuggable: Debugging works with saved .R and .py files
debug.saveFirst: Save the file first to set breakpoints
debug.noBreakpoints: No breakpoints in this file — it will run to the end
debug.pyUnavailable: The Python debugger could not start (needs ipykernel 6+ with debugpy)
debug.breakpointHover: Breakpoint on line {{line}} — click to remove

repro.title: Reproducibility
repro.noProjectBody: Open a project folder to check how reproducible it is and export it.
repro.headlineBody: The bundle pins exact package versions, checksums every file and includes a script that rebuilds the environment and reruns the analysis.

check.pinned: {{count}} packages pinned ({{direct}} used directly, the rest are dependencies)
check.dataOk: Every referenced file is in the project
check.noGitBody: Initialize a repository in the Git panel to record which version was exported

repro.exportWithErrors: You can export now; the guide in the bundle lists the problems above.
repro.insideProject: Choose a folder outside the project

issue.setwd: setwd()/chdir() ties the code to one folder — use project-relative paths
issue.absolutePath: Absolute path “{{detail}}” will not exist on another machine
issue.noSeed: Random numbers ({{detail}}) without a seed — set.seed()/random_state make results repeatable
issue.installInScript: The script installs packages ({{detail}}) — the lockfile does that
issue.missingData: Referenced file “{{detail}}” is not in the project
issue.missingPackage: {{detail}} is used but not installed — it cannot be pinned
issue.uncommitted: {{detail}} uncommitted changes — commit to tie the bundle to a version
issue.noGit: The project is not under version control
issue.githubPackage: {{detail}} is installed from a remote, not a package repository (pinned by commit)

extensions.emptyBody: Install a .dfext package, or load an extension folder while you develop it. The examples/extensions folder of DataForge has a complete example.
extensions.sandboxNote: Extensions run in an isolated worker: they reach your project, kernels and editor only through the permissions you approved.
extensions.uninstallBody: The extension and its files are removed.
extensions.removeDevBody: The folder stays on disk; DataForge just stops loading it.
extensions.noPermissions: • no access to your project, kernels or editor (commands, panels, themes and snippets only)
extensions.needsConsent: Waiting for your approval of its permissions.

perm.editor: Read the selection and text of the active editor, and insert text
perm.kernel: Run R/Python code in your console sessions
perm.workspace: Read the files of the open project (read-only)

extensions.invalidFolder: This folder has no valid dataforge-extension.json
extensions.panelEmpty: The extension has not shown anything here yet.
extensions.keyClash: {{name}}: the shortcut {{keys}} is already used by DataForge and was left out

themes.title: Colour themes
themes.hint: Imports DataForge themes and VS Code colour themes (.json); unreadable colours are fixed to WCAG AA.
themes.adjusted_one: {{count}} colour was adjusted for readability (WCAG AA).
themes.adjusted_other: {{count}} colours were adjusted for readability (WCAG AA).

remote.title: Remote hosts (SSH)
remote.name: Name
remote.hostHint: Host name, IP address or a Host alias from ~/.ssh/config. You can also type user@host:port.
remote.identityHint: Optional: keys from ssh-agent and ~/.ssh/config work too.
remote.deleteBody: Only the saved entry is removed; nothing changes on the remote host.
remote.noInterpreters: No R or Python found on the host.
remote.emptyBody: Add an SSH host to develop remotely.
remote.note: Uses your system ssh client (keys, ssh-agent, ~/.ssh/config, jump hosts). DataForge never stores passwords; the terminal may ask for one.
remote.unknownProfile: Unknown host: {{id}} (its saved entry is missing)
remote.projectOffline: The host of {{name}} is not reachable
remote.kernelNotConnected: The remote host is not reachable
remote.noInterpreter: No {{lang}} kernel on the remote host
remote.lspUnavailable: Not available for remote or shared folders (language servers run locally)
remote.previewUnavailable: Preview is not available for remote or shared folders yet: rendering runs locally.
remote.rDebugUnavailable: The R debugger is not available for remote or shared folders yet (the Python debugger works for remote folders).

err.hostInvalid: Invalid host name (no spaces, @ or leading dash).
err.portInvalid: The port is a whole number between 1 and 65535.

collab.shareIntro: Others can edit the project's files with you in real time, see your cursor and, depending on their role, run code in your kernels. Files and kernels stay on your machine.
collab.joinIntro: Paste the invitation you got from the person sharing. The project stays on their machine; you work with it through the interface.
collab.reachLocalHint: From another computer through an SSH tunnel (ssh -L). The safest choice.
collab.reachLanHint: Anyone on the network who has the invitation.
collab.lanWarning: Traffic on the local network is not encrypted. Only use it on a trusted network, and treat the invitation like a password.

roleHint.view: sees everything: files, cursors, console, variables
roleHint.edit: can also edit and save files
roleHint.run: can also run code in your kernels – that means anything your user account can do; only give it to people you trust

collab.emptyBody: Share your project or join someone else's session: co-editing with live cursors, a shared console and chat.
collab.lanHint: On the network: {{address}}. Anyone who gets it can join; set their role here.
collab.localHint: Reachable from this computer only. From another one: ssh -L {{port}}:127.0.0.1:{{port}} <this computer>, then the invitation works as is.
collab.waiting: Nobody has joined yet. Send the invitation.
collab.removeBody: They leave the session right away. They can rejoin with the invitation until you start a new session.
collab.needProject: Open a project first: that is what gets shared.
collab.alreadyGuest: You can't share as a guest; leave the session first.
collab.endedProjectChanged: Sharing ended because you switched to another project
collab.notThisSession: This file belongs to another session
collab.removed: The host removed you from the session
collab.connectionLost: The connection to the host was lost

err.name: Enter your name: this is how the others see you.

collab.cannotRun: Your role ({{role}}) cannot run code – ask the host for the "Runner" role.

stan.statusHint: The Stan compiler (stanc3) checks the model as you type.
stan.fixErrorsFirst: Fix the model's errors first: the template is built from the data block.
stan.pedanticOn: Pedantic checks on: also warns about common modelling pitfalls.

jobs.title: Background jobs
jobs.emptyBody: An R script or Stan sampling run as a background job runs independently of the console, and keeps running when you close the app or the SSH connection drops.
jobs.lostHint: the process disappeared (e.g. the machine restarted) without reporting the end
jobs.divergencesLong_one: {{count}} divergent transition after warmup. Increase adapt_delta (e.g. 0.95) or reparameterize the model (non-centered).
jobs.divergencesLong_other: {{count}} divergent transitions after warmup. Increase adapt_delta (e.g. 0.95) or reparameterize the model (non-centered).
jobs.treedepthLong_one: {{count}} transition hit the maximum tree depth: efficiency suffers; raise max_treedepth or look at the posterior geometry.
jobs.treedepthLong_other: {{count}} transitions hit the maximum tree depth: efficiency suffers; raise max_treedepth or look at the posterior geometry.
jobs.offline: Connection lost – the jobs keep running on the server. Following resumes automatically once it is reachable again.
jobs.startFailed: The background job did not start
jobs.notInSession: As a guest in a shared session you can't start background jobs (the project is on the host's machine).
jobs.intro: Runs in a separate R process on the project's machine. The console stays free, and the job keeps running when you close the app or the connection drops; when you come back, it is followed here again.
jobs.noDataObjects: There is no list or data frame in the R console. If the model has a data block, first run the code that builds the data list in the console (e.g. stan_data <- list(...)), or copy the data template from the Stan toolbar.
jobs.dataHint: The chosen object is saved when the job starts; later changes to it don't count.
jobs.resultName: Name of the fit when loading
jobs.keepHint: At the end every object the script created (e.g. the brms model) is saved and can be loaded into the console with one click.

err.chains: Chains must be a whole number from 1 to 128.
err.parallel: Parallel chains must be a whole number from 1 to 128.
err.iter: Iterations must be positive whole numbers.
err.seed: The seed is a non-negative whole number (or empty).
err.treedepth: max_treedepth must be a whole number from 1 to 30.
err.refresh: Progress every must be a positive whole number.
err.resultName: Use a valid R variable name (e.g. fit).
